title: Lay a cable cover over the cable where the walkway crosses it
context: A cable across a floor is a trip hazard where people walk over it. Event crews and site electricians put a cover over the crossing, not just anywhere along the cable. Nothing in the instruction says where: the robot has to see where the marked walkway crosses the cable.
setup: A flat black cable (1.2 cm wide, 2 mm thick, 40 cm long) is taped along the table's front-to-back direction on the midline, from 11 to 51 cm in front of the arm bases. A walkway is marked across it: a dark grey card band 14 cm deep (29 to 43 cm from the bases) and 36 cm wide, centred on the midline, with a white tape line on each long edge. A cable cover, a yellow-orange plastic bar (18 x 5 x 2.2 cm, 0.12 kg, long side front to back), lies 15 cm right of the midline with its centre 18 cm from the bases, clear of the walkway.
scoring: Scored at the end. 0 unless the cover is at rest and flat on the table, its long side within 15 degrees of the cable's direction, with its centre within 1.9 cm (left to right) of the cable's centre line and between 11 and 51 cm from the bases. Then 1.0 if its centre is also within 1.5 cm left to right of the cable and within 2 cm front to back of the walkway's centre (36 cm from the bases), so it spans the whole walkway depth; 0.5 if it covers the cable anywhere else along it.
fidelity: Rigid bodies only. The cable is a flat 2 mm fixed strip with no cable physics, and the cover is a plain bar without a channel, so it rests on the cable and the table. Every surface has the same rubber-like friction (1.2).
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (cover not laid on the cable in 600 steps); demo: 1.0 (194 steps)
